title: Comparing three gynoecia
body: A student cut open the ovaries of three flowers during a practical class and recorded what she saw. Flower X (lotus): there are many carpels in the flower and each carpel is free from the others. Flower Y (china rose): the carpels are fused into one ovary that has several chambers; the ovules are attached to a placenta running along the central axis of the ovary. Flower Z (sunflower): the ovary has a single chamber, and one ovule is attached to a placenta that develops at the base of the ovary. She now wants to name the condition of the carpels and the type of placentation in each flower correctly.
